title: SYNTHETIC EXAMPLE — Security Classification Guide for the LANTERN Training Sensor (NOT REAL GUIDANCE)
subject: The fictional LANTERN training sensor, invented to demonstrate the OpenSCG format.
scope: Applies only to this demonstration. Contains no real classification guidance and must not be used to classify anything.
introduction: This synthetic guide shows each kind of OpenSCG entry: an unclassified element, classified elements, a level range with conditions, an exemption, and a compilation.

entries.description: The program name LANTERN and the fact that the program exists.

statements.unclassified: The name is used in public outreach material.

entries.description: The identity of the sponsoring office.
The maximum detection range of the sensor, stated as a specific figure.

reason.explanation: Synthetic rationale: knowing the exact range would let an adversary plan to stay just outside it.

statements.damage: Synthetic: an adversary could avoid detection.

entries.description: The operating frequency band of the sensor.

level_range.condition_text: Unclassified when stated only as a general band name. Confidential when stated to within 10 MHz.

reason.explanation: Synthetic rationale: a precise band would make the sensor easier to jam.

entries.description: Specific conditions under which the sensor fails to detect a target.

reason.explanation: Synthetic rationale: describes a vulnerability of the system.

declassification.event_text: Retirement of the last fielded LANTERN unit, as announced by the program office.

entries.description: The sponsoring office together with the operating band, in the same document.
entries.condition_text: Both items appear together in a way that associates the band with this sponsor.

reason.explanation: Synthetic rationale: together they reveal a mission focus that neither reveals alone.

entries.notes: Each item alone keeps its own level; this entry applies only to the combination.
